title: Maxillary sinus puncture
what: The doctor makes a small hole with a thin needle through the nose into the sinus and rinses it. This lets the pus out.
why: For sinusitis with pus when medicines do not help, or to take a sample for testing.
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to numbing medicine
If you have heart disease or high blood pressure

prepare.title: Scan
prepare.text: An X-ray or CT scan of the sinuses is usually done first.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can have a light meal beforehand.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your medicines on your own. Tell the doctor.

steps: The doctor numbs your nose with a spray or a cotton pad
You sit with your head tilted a little
A thin needle is passed through the wall of the sinus
The sinus is rinsed with a solution through the needle
Fluid and pus drain out through your nose into a tray
feel: The numbing medicine stings a little
During the puncture, you hear a crunch and feel pressure
Rinsing feels like fullness in your cheek
after: A little blood from the nose usually stops quickly
Do not blow your nose hard for the first few hours
Further rinses and medicines are as your doctor prescribes
red_flags: Swelling of the cheek or eyelids, or eye pain
A fever over 38°C after the procedure
A severe headache or vomiting: call emergency services

faq.q: If I have one puncture, will I always need them?
faq.a: No. This is a myth. A puncture does not make you dependent on it.
With numbing medicine, it usually does not hurt, but it is unpleasant.

reminders.text: Sinus puncture tomorrow. Bring your sinus scans and tissues.
